scope: Independent algebra, domain, source and linked-size review of five isolated shared-math variants. No implementation edits; no production acceptance.

algebra.E: sum(k=0..14,r^k/(k+1)!) approximates expm1(r)/r; multiplication by r supplies expm1. Procedural term recurrence multiplies by r/(k+1).
algebra.L: sum(k=0..12,z^k/(2k+1)) approximates atanh(t)/t with z=t*t. Procedural term recurrence multiplies by z*(2k-1)/(2k+1). The log wrapper multiplies by 2*t and adds split n*ln(2).
algebra.bernstein: Exact-rational affine power substitution and degree-n Bernstein conversion agree with independently expanded power coefficients for E, L and the unscaled sqrt seed polynomial. sqrt(2.5) coefficient scaling is rounded to double, so exact equality does not assert floating-point equivalence.
algebra.sqrt: Seed is sqrt(2.5)*sum(k=0..7,binom(1/2,k)*u^k), u=(m-2.5)/2.5. Bernstein maps u in [-0.6,0.6] to (m-1)/3. Odd positive or negative exponent is reduced to an even exponent by doubling m and decrementing exponent; then 3 Newton steps and exponent/2 scaling are consistent. Subnormal preprocessing and output scaling are retained.
algebra.coefficient_storage: Bernstein and Horner seed variants store 15+13+8 binary64 coefficients, 288 B payload. Bernstein without seed stores 224 B. Procedural variant has no coefficient LUT but still has scalar constants and core configuration tables.
algebra.finding: No algebra defect found in reviewed generated sources.

domains.E: exp reduction is approximately [-ln(2)/2,ln(2)/2]; direct expm1 uses |x|<0.5; tanh small branch uses 0<=2*|x|<0.5. All lie within the Bernstein interval [-0.5,0.5].
domains.L: log normalizes m approximately into [1/sqrt(2),sqrt(2)], hence |t|<=about0.171573; direct atanh small branch uses |x|<0.25. Both squares lie in [0,1/16].
domains.sqrt: Positive finite input after subnormal normalization yields m in [1,4); seed input is u in [-0.6,0.6). Existing NaN, negative, zero and infinity handling remains.
domains.helpers: tm_scale is a bounded internal helper, not a fully general ldexp implementation. tm_nextup assumes nonnegative finite cost and direction +infinity. These inherited caller contracts are not widened by this experiment.

memory_interpretation: All allocated instruction, constant, vector and writable-state sections plus alignment are included in the SRAM address span. Current images have no .data payload; in-place initialized data is therefore not double-counted.

All variants retain 4762 B of unique software-double helper symbol ranges including comparison implementations and subtraction wrapper; aliases are merged by address interval. This is a symbol subset rather than an independent whole-program allocation, and is already included in .text.

The procedural variant is smallest among the new variants at 25960 B, but it is 32 B larger than baseline. Bernstein is +40 B, Horner+seed +224 B and Bernstein+seed +304 B. There is no measured SRAM improvement.

Bernstein sm_eval has a 120 B automatic array and compiler-reported frame 168 B (without seed) or160 B (with seed). Horner+seed frame is24 B. These are per-function frame figures, not maximum call-chain stack.

The common1024 B stack amount is an allowance, not variant-specific measured or proven stack. Original baseline stack observations cannot establish stack for new variants. Platform, interrupt, scheduling, persistence and application code remain excluded.

independent_controls.scope: 20000 deterministic random positive finite bit patterns plus exponent/subnormal/end-point neighbors for sqrt/log; arbitrary-scale hypot pairs; exp reduction and overflow/underflow boundary neighbors; wrapper branches, NaNs, infinities, poles and signed zeros.
independent_controls.limits: Python host math references and deterministic finite samples; not correct-rounding proof, exhaustive domain bound, target execution or cycle measurement.

findings.finding: New evaluators change local stack materially. Whole-link with1024B remains a provisional accounting comparison.
findings.disposition: Accept for isolated negative size comparison; require variant-specific target stack evidence or call-chain bounds before any resource qualification.

findings.finding: run.py records one synthetic fixture and host math grids without acceptance thresholds; hypot grid fixes y=1 and does not cover general near-overflow/subnormal pairs. It does not execute new target math instructions.
findings.disposition: Independent boundary/random controls broaden host evidence; retain finite-grid, single-fixture and host-only limits. Require target execution, meaningful tolerances, readout/derivative and longer paired behavior controls before promoting any variant.

findings.finding: Baseline E is degree12 (degree13 expm1), while new E is degree14 (degree15 expm1); baseline log L degree10 changes to degree12. Baseline-vs-shared differences therefore combine evaluation strategy and truncation degree.
findings.disposition: Do not attribute differences solely to sharing or Bernstein form. Bernstein+seed and Horner+seed use matched degrees and normalization, providing the direct evaluator control.

findings.finding: Every new variant enlarges the complete SRAM image and retains the same unique double-helper payload; table removal alone is insufficient for this implementation.
findings.disposition: Preserve as a negative local result. This neither proves a universal lower bound nor excludes different approximation families or data representations.

not_established: lifetime numerical stability or calibrated coverage
general superiority of any polynomial basis
reviewed_result_scope: Only attempt001 and source hashes recorded above. Substantive subsequent implementation changes require new independent review.
